summary: Completed the target-side half of the worker-panic consequence chain. The snapshot pool marks a worker busy and its cluster in progress before handing out a save, recover or stream job, and clears both only in the completion handler that runs after the job function returns. A job that ends in a panic never returns, so that worker stays busy and is skipped for the rest of the process, the cluster stays marked in progress and every later save, recover or stream for it is refused, and with a fixed pool size repeated events exhaust the pool for all clusters; the completion handler also has no idle sweep that could repair a leaked marker. This is target code and holds whenever the goroutine stops without completing, so it is recorded as a Behavior and stated in the worker-panic account ahead of the dependency link, which still decides whether the process survives to experience the leak. That question stays conditional with no defect claim, and the snapshot-save question continues to rest on the same dependency.
